reason: The premise suggests that if Asia has the highest number of child workers and Sub-Saharan Africa has a child labor issue, then Sub-Saharan Africa must have a child worker population. This aligns with the contradiction pattern of factual causation, as it implies a direct causal relationship that may not hold true given the complexities of child labor issues across regions.
refined_position: Causal Misinterpretation - The assumption that a child labor issue in Sub-Saharan Africa necessarily implies a child worker population overlooks the complexities and variances in child labor dynamics across different regions.
